phase: Existing-character migration before further GPU coverage expansion

authority.rule: CPU agreement is regression evidence, not the definition of correct gameplay.
authority.mechanic_evidence: Record game version/date, skill or boss context, reproducible observations or a specific source, and unresolved alternatives.
authority.cpu_disagreement: If evidence contradicts CPU behavior, add an independently expected case and correct the reference and GPU behavior; record the intentional departure from the previous CPU result.
authority.unknown_behavior: Keep an explicit model label. Do not invent an in-game rule or remove a comparison merely to obtain a passing result.
authority.current_change: No newly verified gameplay departure is introduced by this structural migration. Existing parity assertions remain.

common_contract.effect_identity: Definition, source owner, instance and name are distinct identities. Named removal or discharge must specify owner/name scope.
common_contract.targets: Resolution time, living-state filtering and ordered or duplicate targets are explicit per operation. Do not globally deduplicate target lists.
common_contract.events: Preserve authored order, event sequence, nested continuations and whether values are observed before or after HP changes. Ordering changes require interaction tests.
common_contract.conditions: Distinguish activation conditions, live conditions and frozen query results. A condition must not be re-evaluated opportunistically at a different stage.
common_contract.values: Specify units, source/recipient, snapshot time or live evaluation, clamps and rounding groups. Imported ammo/charge option groups remain separate.
common_contract.lifetime: Activation, reapplication, stacking, capacity changes, expiry, explicit removal, down and revival have separate transitions. Shared lifecycle conventions must preserve each operation's transitions.
common_contract.resources: HP, cover, shield, decoy, overheal buffer, healing-charge pool and damage accumulators are distinct resources. Similar storage does not imply identical rules.
common_contract.unsupported: A known semantic family does not authorize compilation. Existing strict compiler rejection and visible CPU fallback stay in force.

implemented_now: One semantic family registry for all parsed skill definitions
One Python source for coarse/detailed numeric stat identities and scoped-inert classification
One ordered entry point for existing CPU reference compatibility layers
One checked source-rewrite utility for storage/sharing/charge reference extensions, preserving each semantic transformer and its expected edit counts
Before/after acceptance and compiled-program comparison across the existing catalog contexts
One recovery verification session with exact-case execution reuse and per-case audit records
Fast, recovery and full test selections with separate reports
Sealed lifecycle operation catalog with explicit CPU phases and dependency order
Per-manager resource state and one synchronous nested-event adapter
Existing shield, decoy, storage, sharing and charge migrated before adding any characters
Generated CUDA activation, retirement and before-body-heal dispatch from the shared lifecycle catalog
Independent old/new CPU complete-squad comparison plus focused state/order witnesses
deliberately_not_changed: CUDA instruction ABI and state layout
Existing arithmetic and authored event ordering
Existing independent comparator and mathematical witness checks
Underlying generic battle interpreter; this migration unifies registered state hooks rather than every battle operation
next_migration_gates: Verify migrated existing characters on native and portable GPU backends before expanding character coverage
Use data-only additions when existing operations suffice; do not add character-name execution branches
Register genuinely new mechanics with explicit phases, dependencies, CPU and GPU handlers, state retention and game evidence
Generate CUDA hooks and rebuild; reject missing CPU registrations or stale generated source
Add independent numerical and event-order/interaction witnesses for new semantics, reusing existing comparator cases
Run the unique full regression set when shared execution or an unknown impact scope changes

test_reuse.lifetime: Current process only; no persistent previous-run result cache
test_reuse.invalidation: Relevant source/data file changes and CPU reference callable rebinding clear reuse.
test_reuse.assertions: Reuse a successful comparison result only for the identical comparator/input/witness combination; return a copy so later assertions cannot modify cached evidence.
test_reuse.unknown_change_scope: Use full regression selection; do not infer independence from a family label alone.

phase_order: Activation: storage/charge snapshots occur before stat-applied notifications.
Protection initialization: after the original stat-applied stage; reuse already resolved targets.
Shield notification: initialize all target capacities and current values before ordered unique shield-applied delivery.
Body heal: freeze sharing allocation, collect charge for each allocated portion, apply storage/clamp, commit HP, then sync HP.
Notify: push event context, run before-notify hooks, complete nested delivery synchronously, restore parent context in finally.
Removal: retain an ended charge pool until discharge consumes it; remove other inactive resource records according to policy.
Down: preserve the base removal/revival behavior and discard inactive owned ledgers only where registered.
Post-notify collection: only collect retained resources when their registered completion predicate permits it; earlier sibling notifications in bulk expiry cannot discard pending charge pools.
lifecycle_runtime.state_identity: One RuntimeState per battle manager; separate resource kind maps keyed by existing active-buff UID. Compatibility attributes refer to the same records.
lifecycle_runtime.registration: Install once and seal the catalog before battle execution. Reject missing handlers, duplicate providers, invalid dependencies and stale generated CUDA.
lifecycle_runtime.gpu_layout: Existing fixed GPU state arrays and ABI remain; generated dispatch replaces scattered lifecycle hook calls. This is not a unified CPU/GPU memory representation.
limits: Base generic battle interpreter remains in place.
A new numeric operation may require compiler/schema/state-layout work beyond registering lifecycle hooks.
A new callback phase requires an explicit executor/generator change and ordering tests.
Current lifecycle policies are regression-tested reference models; game evidence remains a separate requirement.
